summary: Czech police publish every year, for each offence, how many cleared offences were committed by foreigners, including sexual abuse of a child, child pornography, grooming and endangering a child's upbringing. That is a two-way citizenship proxy for perpetrators only; no victims are published by citizenship and ethnicity is never recorded.

nations.National (Police, MPSV, Interior Ministr: Police crime tables by Criminal Code paragraph; child-protection and trafficking reports.

european_title: Not recorded by any Czech source
european_note: Czech crime statistics separate only offences committed by foreigners (people without Czech citizenship) from the rest. Foreigners are mostly Europeans (Slovaks and Ukrainians are the largest groups) and Czech citizens include naturalised immigrants, so ethnic Europeans cannot be identified.
proxy_note: Czechia records citizenship only, never ethnicity. Every group below is a proxy, not ethnicity.

harms.label: Sexual abuse of a child (§187, cleared offences)
harms.intro: From 2025 the Czech Criminal Code has a separate offence of sexual abuse of a child (§187): police registered 645 and cleared 376 in 2025, 13 of them committed by foreigners. Rape (§185: 764 cleared, 109 by foreigners) and sexual assault (§185a: 186 / 24) are not split by victim age. No victims by citizenship.

victims.text: Police statistics publish no victim citizenship; the MPSV child-protection report records no nationality.

perpetrators.scope: Czechia, sexual abuse of a child (§187), offences cleared in 2025
perpetrators.share_note: Police TSK table 2025: offences cleared in the year (objasněno) and, of those, offences committed by foreigners (spácháno cizinci); counts are offences, not persons, and include all victim ages unless the offence is child-specific. Citizenship, a proxy, not ethnicity: 'foreigners' (cizinci) are people without Czech citizenship, including Slovaks and Ukrainians; Czech citizens include naturalised immigrants.

cross.text: No victim data by citizenship, so nothing can be linked.

breakdown.why: The Police of the Czech Republic's annual crime table (TSK, 2025) gives, for sexual abuse of a child (§187: 645 registered, 376 cleared), the number of cleared offences committed by foreigners (13). Czech/foreign only, offences not persons, no nationality, no victims by citizenship.

TSK gives cleared offences and those by foreigners for maltreatment of a person in care (§198: 162 / 23) and in a shared home (§199: 394 / 55), all victim ages. The MPSV child-protection report (V20-01) counts physical abuse cases with no citizenship.

TSK gives endangering a child's upbringing (§201: 1,116 cleared, 138 by foreigners). The MPSV child-protection report records neglect cases but only flags foreign children with registered residence and unaccompanied foreign minors, not the nationality of neglected children.
TSK gives all murders (§140: 148 cleared, 28 by foreigners), all victim ages; no child homicide breakdown and no victims by citizenship.

TSK gives trafficking (§168: 22 cleared, 2 by foreigners). The Interior Ministry's support programme lists its 31 new victims in 2025 by citizenship (27 Czech), but it admits adults only; its 2024 report gives 28 people prosecuted (26 Czech citizens).
TSK gives child pornography (§192/193: 705 cleared, 32 by foreigners) and grooming (§193b: 45 cleared, 4 by foreigners). No victims by citizenship.

components.name: Victim heritage
components.full: Official data by harm that separately identify ethnic European children (e.g. White non-Hispanic, White British) alongside every other group, self-reported or official, few unknowns. Broad categories that lump ethnic Europeans with others get partial credit; proxies (nationality, citizenship, migration background, country of birth) at most 9.4 points.

components.name: Perpetrator heritage
components.full: Same standard for perpetrators: not perceived, few unknowns, ethnic Europeans separately identified. Proxies at most 9.4 points.

components.name: Coverage and missing data
components.full: Over 90% of the population covered, under 10% unknown

components.name: Rates and linkage
components.full: Rates per 100,000 possible, and victim heritage linked to perpetrator heritage

score.gold_standard: 100% means a country publishes data that separately identifies ethnic Europeans, both as perpetrators (so one can tell when they disproportionately harm a group) and as child victims (so one can tell when ethnic European children are disproportionately harmed), alongside every other group, linked victim to perpetrator, for every harm.
score.rules: Heritage is 75 of every 100 points (victims 37.5, perpetrators 37.5); coverage, rates and access share the other 25. Proxies such as nationality or migration background earn at most a quarter of the heritage points. A country with no real ethnicity data for victims or perpetrators is capped at 25%.
score.why: Czechia scores 11% on the stricter scale (0-20%). The police publish an annual table of every offence with the number of cleared offences committed by foreigners, including sexual abuse of a child, child pornography, grooming and endangering a child's upbringing. That is a two-way Czech/foreign citizenship proxy for perpetrators only, counted in offences, with no nationality detail and no victims by citizenship.
score.weights_id: harm weights of 19 Nov 2026 (homicide 25, sexual abuse 20, sex trafficking 20, physical abuse 15, online exploitation 10, neglect 10)
